## Purpose

This procedure describes the determination of soil labile amino-nitrogen
(amino-N) using the Solvita SLAN test (Woods End Laboratories)
[@brinton2016slan]. The SLAN test measures a chemically labile fraction
of organic nitrogen present in soil humus as amino-sugars and related
amino compounds. These forms represent a "potentially available"
nitrogen pool that lies between the immediately available mineral
nitrogen (NH~4~^+^ and NO~3~^-^) measured by conventional extraction
and the total nitrogen pool measured by combustion or Kjeldahl
digestion.

The test uses alkali hydrolysis with 2 mol L^-1^ NaOH to release NH~3~
from amino-N compounds in soil [@mulvaney2001]. The liberated NH~3~
diffuses into a Solvita gel probe during a 24-hour room-temperature
incubation. The color change of the gel is proportional to the quantity
of labile amino-N and is quantified using the Solvita Digital Color
Reader (DCR) in NH~3~ mode, yielding results in mg kg^-1^ amino-N.

The SLAN procedure is chemically analogous to the Illinois Soil Nitrogen
Test (ISNT), which uses the same 2 mol L^-1^ NaOH reagent but requires
heating. The SLAN test offers two practical advantages over the ISNT:
heating is not needed, and fewer reagents are required
[@moore2019correlations]. In combination with the Solvita CO~2~ Burst
test ([SOP-L408](SOP-L408-solvita-co2-burst.qmd)), SLAN provides a
complementary assessment of biological soil fertility by pairing a
measure of microbial activity (CO~2~ respiration) with a measure of
organic nitrogen reserves [@brinton2016proficiency].

This SOP is distinct from [SOP-L408](SOP-L408-solvita-co2-burst.qmd),
which measures microbial CO~2~ respiration from rewetted soil, and from
[SOP-L403](SOP-L403-nitrate-ammonium-kcl.qmd), which measures
immediately available mineral nitrogen by KCl extraction.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Air-dried, sieved mineral soils from all EA Program
  sites; assessment of organic nitrogen reserves and humus quality;
  screening for management effects on labile nitrogen pools
- **Does not apply to:** Measurement of immediately available mineral
  nitrogen (NH~4~^+^ or NO~3~^-^; see
  [SOP-L403](SOP-L403-nitrate-ammonium-kcl.qmd) or
  [SOP-L404](SOP-L404-nitrate-quick-test.qmd)); total soil nitrogen
  determination (see [SOP-L407](SOP-L407-total-carbon.qmd) and elemental
  analysis); compost maturity testing (see
  [SOP-L413](SOP-L413-solvita-compost-maturity.qmd)); field-moist soils
  (samples must be air-dried before testing)
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133

## Definitions

- **Alkali-hydrolyzable nitrogen (AHN):** The fraction of organic
  nitrogen released by hydrolysis in sodium hydroxide solution;
  operationally defined by the extraction conditions; highly correlated
  with amino acid nitrogen and microbially available N [@mulvaney2001].
- **Amino acid nitrogen:** Organic nitrogen in the form of free amino
  acids and simple peptides; the most labile fraction of soil organic
  nitrogen; the primary substrate measured by the Solvita SLAN test.
- **Diffusion cell:** The sealed incubation jar used in the Solvita SLAN
  test in which NaOH releases NH~3~ from hydrolyzed soil nitrogen into
  the headspace, where it is captured and measured by a gel probe.
- **Digital Color Reader (DCR):** The Solvita handheld device that reads
  gel probe color and converts it to a numerical amino-N concentration
  (mg kg^-1^); set to NH~3~ mode for SLAN measurements.
- **Gel probe (SLAN):** The colorimetric sensor in the Solvita SLAN test
  that changes color in proportion to accumulated NH~3~; read with the
  DCR after exactly 24 hours of incubation.
- **Labile amino nitrogen (LAN):** The nitrogen fraction estimated by
  the Solvita SLAN test; a proxy for readily mineralizable organic
  nitrogen; expressed as mg N kg^-1^ dry soil [@moore2019labile].
- **Nitrogen mineralization:** The biological conversion of organic
  nitrogen to inorganic forms (NH~4~^+^ and eventually NO~3~^-^) by soil
  microorganisms; the primary process by which plant-available N is
  replenished from organic matter; positively correlated with LAN
  [@moore2019correlations].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) at 2 mol L^-1^ is strongly
  corrosive and can cause severe burns to skin, eyes, and mucous
  membranes. Handle with care; refer to the NaOH Safety Data Sheet (SDS)
  posted in the lab. The SLAN test requires use of a strong reagent and
  is not intended for casual or unsupervised use.
- **Biological:** Soil samples may contain soil-borne pathogens. Wash
  hands thoroughly after handling soil.
- **Physical:** Minor risk of glass breakage from incubation jars.
  Handle jars carefully.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (chemical-resistant)
- [ ] Safety glasses or splash goggles
- [ ] Lab coat

### Emergency Procedures

- For NaOH contact with skin, immediately flush the affected area with
  copious water for at least 15 minutes. Remove contaminated clothing.
- For NaOH contact with eyes, flush with water at the eyewash station
  for at least 15 minutes and seek medical attention.
- For spills, neutralize with dilute acid (e.g., 0.1 M HCl or vinegar)
  or contain with absorbent material, then clean up and dispose per
  institutional guidelines.
- Refer to [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
  for general emergency procedures.


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                                      |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Solvita SLAN test kit                 | Includes NH~3~ gel probes, incubation jars with silicone-gasketed lids, 50 mL plastic beakers, color chart, and manual |
| Solvita Digital Color Reader (DCR)    | Set to NH~3~ mode; calibrate per manufacturer instructions |
| Incubation jars (~250 mL)            | Glass with silicone-gasketed screw-top lids; provided with kit |
| Analytical balance (0.01 g)           | See [SOP-L102](SOP-L102-using-balances.qmd) |
| Graduated cylinder (25 or 50 mL)     | For dispensing NaOH solution               |
| Timer                                 | 24-hour countdown                          |
| Lab notebook or data sheet            | For recording results                      |

### Consumables and Reagents

| Item                                  | Notes                                      |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Solvita NH~3~ gel probes              | One per test; store sealed at room temperature in the dark; check expiration dates |
| 50 mL plastic beakers (cups)          | Provided with kit; one per test            |
| Sodium hydroxide (NaOH), 2 mol L^-1^ | Prepare from ACS-grade NaOH pellets; see Section 5.1 |

### Reagent Preparation

**2 mol L^-1^ NaOH solution:**

1. Weigh 80.0 g of ACS-grade NaOH pellets.
2. Dissolve in approximately 800 mL of deionized water in a 1 L
   volumetric flask or heat-resistant beaker. The dissolution is
   exothermic; add pellets slowly and stir.

::: {.callout-warning}
Always add NaOH to water, never water to NaOH. Use a heat-resistant
container and allow the solution to cool to room temperature before
bringing to final volume.
:::

3. Bring to a final volume of 1000 mL with deionized water.
4. Transfer to a labeled, tightly sealed polyethylene bottle. NaOH
   solutions absorb CO~2~ from the atmosphere; keep sealed when not in
   use.
5. Label with: reagent name, concentration, date prepared, preparer's
   initials, and expiration date (6 months from preparation).


## Procedure

### Sample Preparation

1. Use soil that has been air-dried and sieved through a 2 mm sieve per
   [SOP-F400](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd). Do not grind
   the soil.
2. If samples were stored at 4 °C after sieving, allow them to
   equilibrate to room temperature (20--25 °C) for at least 30 minutes
   before beginning the assay.
3. Gently mix each sample to ensure homogeneity before weighing.

::: {.callout-note}
The SLAN test is designed for air-dried soil. Results from field-moist
soil are not comparable to published SLAN norms or the manufacturer's
interpretation guidelines [@brinton2016slan].
:::

### Incubation Setup

1. Weigh 4.0 g of air-dried, sieved soil into a clean 50 mL plastic
   beaker. Record the exact mass to 0.01 g.
2. Place the beaker containing soil inside a clean, dry 250 mL
   incubation jar.
3. Using the graduated cylinder, add 20 mL of 2 mol L^-1^ NaOH directly
   to the soil in the beaker.
4. Remove a fresh NH~3~-sensitive gel probe from its sealed foil packet.
   Inspect the gel: it should be uniform in color with no cracks,
   discoloration, or signs of prior exposure. Discard any compromised
   probes.
5. Place the gel probe in the air space surrounding the plastic beaker.
   The gel face must be exposed to the headspace and must not contact
   the NaOH solution or the soil.
6. Seal the jar immediately and securely with the silicone-gasketed lid.
7. Record the jar number, sample ID, soil mass, and start time.

::: {.callout-important}
Work efficiently once the NaOH is added. NH~3~ begins volatilizing
immediately upon contact with the soil; seal the jar as quickly as
possible to capture the full emission.
:::

### Incubation

1. Place sealed jars at room temperature (20--25 °C), shielded from
   direct sunlight and drafts.
2. Incubate undisturbed for 24 hours.
3. Do not open, move, or disturb jars during incubation.

### Reading Results

1. After exactly 24 hours (±30 minutes), open the jar and immediately
   remove the gel probe.
2. Read the probe promptly; prolonged exposure to ambient air will alter
   the gel color.

**Using the Solvita Digital Color Reader (DCR -- recommended):**

3. Set the DCR to NH~3~ mode.
4. Insert the gel probe into the DCR and record the numerical reading.
5. The DCR reading corresponds to amino-N concentration in mg kg^-1^
   per the manufacturer's calibration [@brinton2016slan].

**Using the Solvita Color Chart (visual -- semi-quantitative only):**

3. Compare the gel probe to the Solvita NH~3~ color chart.
4. Record the color number.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip

Read probes within 2 minutes of opening the jar. The DCR is strongly
recommended for all quantitative work; the color chart provides
semi-quantitative screening only.
:::

### Recording Results

Record the following for each test:

- Date and time (start and end of incubation)
- Sample ID, site, and depth
- Soil mass (g)
- NaOH volume added (mL)
- DCR reading (NH~3~ mode) or color chart number
- Amino-N concentration (mg kg^-1^)
- Any anomalies (unusual soil color or odor, probe defects)

### Cleanup

1. Carefully pour the NaOH-soil slurry into the designated waste
   container. Do not pour corrosive solutions down the drain without
   neutralization (see Section 8).
2. Rinse plastic beakers and incubation jars with deionized water. Dry
   completely before reuse.
3. Dispose of used gel probes in standard trash.


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### QC Requirements

| QC Element         | Requirement                                             |
|:-------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Duplicates         | At least 1 per 10 samples; RPD within 15%              |
| Blank              | One jar with 20 mL NaOH, no soil, and a gel probe per batch; probe should show no or minimal color change |
| DCR calibration    | Calibrate per manufacturer instructions before each batch; set to NH~3~ mode |
| Gel probe storage  | Store sealed in foil at room temperature, away from light; check expiration dates; never use expired probes |
| NaOH solution      | Verify 2 mol L^-1^; check expiration; keep tightly sealed |

### Corrective Actions

- If the blank reading exceeds baseline by more than one color
  increment, check for NH~3~ contamination sources (nearby ammonium
  reagents, compost, inadequate ventilation) and repeat the batch.
- If duplicate RPD exceeds 15%, re-run the sample pair. Persistent poor
  precision may indicate sample heterogeneity; increase homogenization
  effort before weighing.
- If NaOH solution appears cloudy or shows precipitate, prepare a fresh
  solution.

### Limitations

The SLAN test does not detect nitrate or urea, and normal ammonium
fertilizer rates do not interfere with the measurement. Known
limitations include:

- The test may not be sensitive in very low-organic-matter soils
  (e.g., sandy soils with less than 1% SOM), where results may fall
  below the detection limit.
- Color matching by visual chart is subjective; the DCR is required for
  quantitative reporting.
- SLAN measures a chemically defined labile N pool, not the
  biologically available fraction directly; interpret alongside other
  soil health indicators.

### Interpretation Guide

| SLAN Amino-N (mg kg^-1^) | Interpretation | Implication                    |
|:--------------------------|:---------------|:-------------------------------|
| Less than 30              | Very low       | Severely depleted organic N reserves; management intervention warranted |
| 30--60                    | Low            | Limited labile N pool; consider cover crops or organic amendments |
| 60--120                   | Moderate       | Adequate organic N reserves for many soils |
| 120--200                  | High           | Good labile N pool; indicative of healthy humus |
| Greater than 200          | Very high      | Abundant organic N reserves; common in high-SOM, no-till, or prairie soils |

*Thresholds are approximate guidelines adapted from Woods End
Laboratories and published field studies [@moore2019predicting; @moore2019labile].
Interpret SLAN values in the context of soil organic matter content,
soil texture, and management history.*

## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                     | Disposal Method                                    |

| Used gel probes                | Standard trash                                     |
| Deionized water rinses         | Drain                                              |
| Incubation jars and beakers    | Wash, rinse with DI water, and reuse               |

## Training Record

Before performing the Solvita SLAN test independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the Solvita SLAN Official Instructions manual (included in
   the kit or available from solvita.com)
4. Demonstrate safe handling and preparation of 2 mol L^-1^ NaOH
   solution
5. Observe a trained operator perform the full procedure from sample
   weighing through DCR reading
6. Perform at least one test under supervision with acceptable QC
   results (duplicate RPD within 15%; blank within acceptable range)
7. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
